instruction.task: Write a very small diagnostic script that prints the current hostname, available rooted servers reachable from home via recursive scan, each server's max money, current money, min security, current security, required hacking level, max RAM, and whether we have root. Sort by max money descending. Exit after printing. Keep RAM usage minimal by avoiding expensive APIs like getServer or hackAnalyzeChance.
instruction.context: We have almost no money after 60 seconds, so we need visibility into what servers exist and which target is best on level 1. Your script should be short-lived and purely diagnostic. Use only cheap APIs such as scan, getHostname, hasRootAccess, getServerMaxMoney, getServerMoneyAvailable, getServerMinSecurityLevel, getServerSecurityLevel, getServerRequiredHackingLevel, getServerMaxRam. Start from home and recursively discover the network while avoiding revisits.

instruction.task: Write a long-running early-game money script optimized for very low RAM. It should recursively scan from home, choose the best rooted target with money and required hacking level at or below our current hacking level, preferring highest max money. Then loop forever on that single target: if security is above min+5, weaken; else if money is below 75% of max, grow; else hack. Re-evaluate target every 30 iterations or if target becomes invalid. Print chosen target and occasional status. Avoid all expensive APIs.
instruction.context: Current money is only 1262 after one minute, so we need a reliable low-RAM earner now. Assume no batching, no purchased servers, and likely only home/rooted starter hosts. Simplicity and actually running are more important than sophistication. Use cheap getters only; do not use getServer, formulas, or hackAnalyzeChance.

instruction.task: Write an ultra-low-RAM long-running income script that does not scan. It should work on a fixed fallback list of common starter hosts plus home, e.g. ['n00dles','foodnstuff','sigma-cosmetics','joesguns','nectar-net','hong-fang-tea','harakiri-sushi','home']. Pick the rooted host from that list with required hacking level <= current hacking level and highest max money, excluding home unless nothing else has money. Then loop forever on that one target: if current security > min security + 5, weaken; else if current money < 75% of max money, grow; else hack. Re-check the best target every 20 loops and switch if a better valid one appears. Print the selected target at start and whenever it changes, plus sparse status every ~25 loops. Avoid recursion and avoid all expensive APIs like getServer or hackAnalyzeChance. Keep the script tiny and robust so it definitely starts under RAM limits.
instruction.context: Our scan-based scout had inconsistent startup and earner1 is still pending. We need a guaranteed tiny earner immediately to maximize money in level 1. Prefer reliability over sophistication. Use only very cheap APIs: hasRootAccess, getHackingLevel, getServerRequiredHackingLevel, getServerMaxMoney, getServerMoneyAvailable, getServerMinSecurityLevel, getServerSecurityLevel, hack, grow, weaken, print/tprint, sleep if needed. No scan, no getHostname, no purchased-server logic, no extra features.

instruction.task: Write a minimal short-lived diagnostic script using a fixed fallback list of common starter hosts instead of scan. It should print one concise line for each rooted host we can currently hack from this list: n00dles, foodnstuff, sigma-cosmetics, joesguns, nectar-net, hong-fang-tea, harakiri-sushi. For each, print hostname, required hacking level, max money, current money percent, and min/current security. Sort by max money descending and tprint every line. Exit immediately after printing.
